summary: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sarah Lawrence College, Harvard University, and Radcliffe College. She held academic posts at Harvard University (~1954–1964) and the University of Chicago (~1964–2003).

Susanne Mrozik is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned an M.T.S. at Harvard University, studying under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey and teachers Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles, later teaching at Western Michigan and Mount Holyoke.

Sushanta Sen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Visva-Bharati University, Sen served there as a lecturer in 1986 and was a lecturer in Indian Religions in the Department of Theology at the University of Birmingham.

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2003) under Makio Takemura, and later held part-time lecturer posts at Kyoto University, Hanazono University, and Bukkyo University.
Susumu Sakurabe is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University from ~1945 to 1948 and later served as a professor there from ~1968 to 1996.

Susumu Shimazono is a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1977). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo as Professor of Religious Studies, and Sophia University.

Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar. Educated at Otani and Kyoto universities under Sylvain Lévi, Louis de La Vallée Poussin, Enga Teramoto, and Gessho Sasaki, he was a long-serving professor at Otani University.

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College. His career includes attested affiliations in 2001 with the University of Toronto and the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies.

Suzanne Karpelès (1890–1968) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1914–1920) and later held a post at the French Information Bureau (~1945–1948).

Suzanne Newcombe is a religious studies and Indology scholar who completed a doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at Cambridge, the London School of Economics, Inform, King's College London, and the Open University.
Sven Wittemann is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Syed Ali Bilgrami (1853–1911) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lucknow, IIT Roorkee, and London. He served in the Government of Hyderabad (~1876–1901) and as Reader in Marathi at the University of Cambridge (~1902–1911).

Syed Hasan Askari (1901–1990) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College, and Patna University, and served as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.
Syed Nawab Ali was a scholar of history who served as Professor of Persian at Baroda College and as Principal of Bahauddin College (both attested 1932).
Sylvain Brocquet is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1980 and held a post at Aix-Marseille University around 2002.

Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied at École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held chairs at the University of Paris, Collège de France, and EPHE.
Sze-bong Tso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he was supervised by Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.
Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was an Indology scholar. During his career, he held posts at the Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen from ~1889 to 1902.

T. Chandrasekharan was an Indology scholar who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at The Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951), where he succeeded T. R. Chintamani.

T. Griffith Foulk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, subsequently teaching at Michigan (~1987–1995) and Sarah Lawrence College (~1995–2012).
